text: Which file is the server-side handler that serves the whole top-level sign-in popup page for the sandbox preview, redirecting straight to the OAuth provider on the first step and then returning a tiny HTML page that sends the session token back to the opener window and closes itself?
why: Only this file implements the two-phase server-only popup document (OAuth redirect plus postMessage-and-close page); the other auth files cover the client opener, session handling, or gate identity, not the popup response itself.

text: Which file implements a testable, side-effect-injected logic for ending a user's session that waits a short time in a sandboxed preview but a much longer time when deployed, throwing an error on failure only in the deployed case, plus a best-effort variant that runs before a new login begins?
why: It is the only file that defines the timeout-bounded sign-out sequence with differing preview versus deployed failure behavior; other auth files and the matching test file do not contain this logic itself.

text: Which file glues the client-side desk state store to the Python/SQLite engine by sending short text commands (canon, raw, plant, accept, take, run, fetch) through the server call and then parsing the tab-separated, JSON or arrow-style output back into store rows, instruments and wires?
why: Only this file wraps the engine command executor with refresh and paired local-plus-database action helpers that parse the engine's output into the desk store, unlike the store, the executor wrapper, or the engine itself.

text: Which file configures the project's linting rules, skipping build output folders and the generated route tree, enabling React hooks and fast-refresh checks, relaxing the unused-variable and explicit-any rules for TypeScript, and finally turning off rules that clash with the code formatter?
why: It is the only ESLint flat config in the repository; no other file sets up linting rules or ignores.

text: Which file defines the SQLite table layout for a local portfolio index, including tables for objects, their links, session origins, an event log, and messages passed between sessions, along with supporting lookup indexes?
why: It is the only SQL schema file for the engine's local SQLite index; the other SQL files are a seed data file and a separate Better Auth migration with user/session/account tables.

text: Which file defines the full-screen fallback view shown when a route throws, displaying a warning icon, a "something went wrong" heading, and the error's message (or a generic retry hint) with light and dark theme styling?
why: It is the only file that renders a router error fallback page; other files handle auth, data, or routing but none render a generic error screen.

text: Which file is the browser-side authentication client that keeps a session-scoped bearer token for the embedded sandbox preview iframe, opens a popup for sign-in there but uses a normal redirect when deployed, and wraps sign-out so the stored token is also cleared?
why: Among the auth files, only this one combines the browser-side client setup, sessionStorage bearer token handling, popup-versus-redirect sign-in logic and the sign-out wrapper, whereas the server popup, gate and session files handle only server-side pieces.

text: Which file implements the third-stage memory page of the web app, showing the stored canon split into subject–object cells, graph edges between packets, and remaining records, with a per-row button that runs an item and then jumps to the fourth-stage page?
why: Only this route page renders the three tables (cells, packet edges, other canon) with a run-and-navigate-to-L4 action, distinguishing it from the sibling stage pages l2, l4 and index.

text: Which file renders the SVG diagram of four stages laid out in switchable geometric arrangements (diamond, figure-eight, isometric), with clickable stage nodes that toggle a stop state and small selectable token dots orbiting each node?
why: It is the only component drawing the interactive SVG cycle with three layout modes, stage nodes with brake toggling, and token dots; the sibling panel, nav and instruments components do not draw this diagram.

text: Which file provides the React components that conditionally render content based on whether a visitor is signed in, signed out, or still loading, plus a redirect to the login route, provider sign-in buttons, and a small user identity chip whose sign-out control is hidden for auto-signed-in gate sessions?
why: It is the only file bundling these UI auth-state wrapper components (signed-in/out gates, redirect, sign-in buttons, user chip), whereas other auth files handle server logic, hooks, or clients.

text: Which file is the command-line script that builds a local SQLite project database from a schema and seed data, then reports status counts, lists open questions and blockers, runs consistency checks, prints next-step rules, and exports a markdown status summary?
why: It is the only Python command-line tool in the catalog operating on the SQLite portfolio store; the other engine files are SQL schema/seed data or markdown docs, and the rest is TypeScript/JS web app code.

text: Which file declares the shared constants and type definitions for calling third-party connector tools, including the supported connector kinds (mail, calendar, drive, chat, etc.), the tool name lists for the Google Drive and Calendar integrations, the header and event names for the access-token handoff, and the result and options shapes for a tool call?
why: It is the only file in the app-data module that purely defines connector type enums, Google Drive/Calendar tool name maps, token header/event constants, and call result/options types, while other app-data files hold logic like client calls, error classification, login redirects, and readiness polling.

text: Which file is a standalone check that compares whether sign-in is enabled on a locally running development server against what the production build would use, exiting with distinct codes for agreement, divergence, or inability to observe?
why: Only this script probes the dev server's resolved auth flag and compares it with the build-time value; its test file and the smoke/wrapper scripts only consume or wrap parts of it.

text: Which file is a short Russian-language reference describing the small command language for a set-based portfolio calculator, covering set union/intersection/difference operations, a ban on multiplying matrices, and bulk macros that accept or take whole sets of items rather than lists pasted from chat?
why: It is the only file defining the calculator's set/matrix operation grammar and macros; the other engine docs (LANG-FROM-DB, CHAT-CRUTCH, README) cover different topics such as database-sourced cells, chat workarounds, and overview.

text: Which file is the SQL script that wipes all portfolio tables and reloads them with the initial canonical set of records about a Kazakhstan employment-service AI case (facts, questions, decisions, observations, signals, links, a handoff packet and a single seeding event)?
why: It is the only file that contains concrete data inserts for the portfolio (the schema file only defines tables), and its content is specifically the Enbek-related canon dated 2026-09-18.

text: Which file is the small React component, mounted once at the app root, that wires the router into the embedding preview chrome so the host can trigger page navigation and read the app's route paths, doing nothing when the app isn't embedded?
why: It is the only component wrapper that installs the host bridge with the router, while the lib file with a similar name holds the underlying postMessage logic rather than a React component.

text: Which file defines the React gauge components that render circular percentage dials for charge, raw versus canon counts, and skew warnings, plus a small cluster-to-cluster packet count table and a one-line compact status summary?
why: It is the only component file combining circular conic-gradient dials, a 4x4 hop matrix table, and a compact instrument readout strip; other components (cycle panel, board, command bar) do not render these gauges.

text: Which file implements the second-stage page of the desk app, showing a filterable grid of raw and canonical database records by cluster and search text, with buttons to run bulk fill, sweep, gap and purge commands and to load the kit's ontology tables into the store?
why: Among the routes, only this one is the second-layer 'plane' page combining cluster filters, a search box, bulk bridge commands, and loading kit ontology JSON, distinct from the L1, L3 and L4 pages.

text: Which file is the build-time script that connects to a Postgres database via the URL in the environment, applies any not-yet-run SQL files from the migrations folder each inside its own transaction while logging them in a bookkeeping table, and quietly exits when no database URL is configured?
why: It is the only node-postgres deploy-time migration runner; other migration-related files only plan which migrations are pending or test that plan, and db.ts handles the embedded PGLite fallback.

text: Which file implements the app's landing page where a user pastes or uploads raw text, sends it to be planted into the database before moving on to the second stage, can reset the working desk, and sees a preview table of the first 40 already-stored raw rows?
why: It is the root route page with the raw text input area, file upload, plant-and-navigate button, and table of stored raw rows, unlike the other stage pages (l2, l3, l4) which handle later steps.

text: Which file verifies short-lived signed identity tokens passed in a request header by the hosting gateway, fetching and caching the gateway's public keys and deciding which issuer to trust based on the request's host, then turns the verified identity into a user-info record with fallback email and name?
why: Only this file combines verifying the gateway's signed identity token via cached public keys, host-based issuer resolution, and mapping to user info; other auth files handle sessions, popups, or cookies around it but not this verification.

text: Which file defines the client-side persisted state store for the desk workflow, holding the pasted tape text, candidate rows that can be accepted or rejected, an event log capped at a fixed length, and a small text-command interpreter (status, look, plant, accept, run, fetch, reset), where only the tape text survives reloads?
why: It is the only file that combines a zustand store with row accept/reject status, event log, command-line interpreter, and partial persistence of just the tape; other stores (cycle-store) and bridges (desk-bridge) lack this combination.

text: Which file splits a pasted chat transcript into blank-line-separated chunks and classifies each chunk heuristically (as a link, a continuation or affirmation, a question, an invariant-style observation, or a numbered section heading) into a structured record with an id, cluster, and type?
why: It is the only file that turns raw pasted chat text into typed records by keyword and regex rules, whereas other files handle storage, UI, or the Python engine.

text: Which file implements the server-side Better Auth plugin logic that turns a Grok gate viewer's identity header into a signed session cookie delivered through both the framework's cookie store and the auth response headers, expires the previous user's cached session data when identities swap, and manages a client-readable marker cookie for gate-created sessions?
why: Only this file handles materializing sessions from the gate identity header with dual-path cookie emission and the marker cookie, whereas gate-identity.server.ts only verifies tokens and gate-session-marker.ts only defines the cookie name.

text: Which file is the generated, do-not-edit SQL migration that creates the tables for users, login sessions, linked provider accounts, and verification tokens, along with lookup indexes on their foreign-key and identifier columns, for the app's sign-in system?
why: It is the only SQL migration in the repo that defines the authentication tables (the other SQL files are the portfolio schema and seed for the engine), so no other file matches.

text: Which file is the static HTML template that detects whether the visitor is on an iPhone, iPad, Android or desktop and shows step-by-step instructions for adding the app to an iOS Home Screen, or on desktop just tells them to open the link on their iOS device?
why: It is the only HTML page in the catalog, and it uniquely contains the device-detection script and Add-to-Home-Screen instructions with app name/URL placeholders.
